이 두 개의 유물은 멸망 이전 인류가 가장 흔하게 지니고 다녔던 쌍둥이: These two relics were twin-like items that humanity carried most commonly before the fall. In one hand was a rectangular slab (smartphone) charged overnight with fingers moving busily, and in the other was a tumbler preserving ice or hot coffee for more than half a day. They boarded crowded trains every morning heading for a place called 'work'. Amid repetitive exhaustion, they merely grumbled, never dreaming that this vast gray city and warm coffee would vanish forever.
Anyone who enters this labyrinth sees the vision they desire most. Deceased family members run forward smiling, and a ruined hometown flourishes brilliantly. Countless expeditions, intoxicated by those sweet illusions, closed their eyes and laid down their blades. But on the reverse of the mirror, the cold fiends of the labyrinth merely smile as they strip the flesh from their bones.
이 손목시계의 초침은 11시 47분 23초에 정확히 얼어붙어 있다. 광화: The second hand of this wristwatch is frozen precisely at 11:47:23. That was the exact moment when the massive subway map connecting Gwanghwamun and Gangnam was crumpled in blood and mud. As mysterious purple black fog poured from the sky, hundreds of thousands of citizens flooded into subway platforms designated as underground shelters. The power failed, emergency lights flickered, doors wouldn't close—terror seized the fleeting instant. The second hand stopped, but traces of their desperate flight remain deeply etched into the bedrock of the 4th basement floor.
